heading: Small-Cap Funds: Understanding Liquidity Risk and Longer Redemption Times
tldr: SEBI data indicates that top small-cap funds can take significantly longer to liquidate half their portfolios compared to mid-cap funds.
Small-cap funds required an average of 51 days to sell half their assets, while mid-cap funds needed only 23 days as per FY26 data.
This extended liquidation period highlights potential redemption risks for investors, especially during market downturns or high outflow periods.
The rapidly growing Assets Under Management (AUM) in small-cap schemes further exacerbates these liquidity concerns.
Investors should carefully monitor fund house stress test reports and consider their investment horizon and risk tolerance for small-cap exposure.
caption:
Ever wondered how quickly your money can come back from an investment? A recent report shows that if you invest in smaller company funds, it might take much longer to get your money out compared to funds investing in bigger companies. This is important to know, especially if markets get shaky. It means you might have to wait longer to access your cash. Learn more about why this matters for your investments.
